subject: Materials Science
title: Protective Coatings: Paint and Beyond
description: A short lesson to help you apply Protective Coatings: Paint and Beyond.

hook.text: The Eiffel Tower needs 60 tons of paint every seven years — without it, rust would eat it alive.

buildup.text: Coatings create a barrier between the metal and its environment — no electrolyte contact, no corrosion.

discovery.text: Epoxy primers, polyurethane topcoats, and zinc-rich base coats work as a system — each layer has a job.

twist.text: A tiny holiday (pinhole) in a coating concentrates corrosion at that spot — worse than no coating at all.

climax.text: Marine coatings must survive salt spray, UV, abrasion, and flexing — a multi-billion dollar industry.

punchline.text: The cheapest corrosion defense is a good coat of paint — applied properly.

quiz.question: Why can a small hole in a coating make corrosion worse?
options: The hole lets in UV light that weakens the metal
Corrosion concentrates at the exposed spot, accelerating local attack
The hole lets paint chemicals corrode the metal
